clips.dynamic: Bach Prelude · edition slurs as hammer-ons and pull-offs
clips.description: Same fitted velocities, timing and measured-body model in both. B plays all six slurs Apke marks as left-hand legato. Hammer-ons (bar 2 E→F♯, bar 8 G♯→B and D♯→E): the ringing string is shortened without a new pluck, and the finger’s slam onto the fret excites it. Pull-offs (bars 4 and 6 E→D♯ on the 2nd string, bar 10 E→D♯ on the 1st): the string lengthens, and the leaving finger plucks it sideways at the old fret, so the note is bright and thin. Each slurred note is matched to its fitted plucked level, so only the articulation differs. Assumption: Kowalski slurs these notes (unverified). Designed physics, not fitted.

clips.dynamic: Bach slurs, slow · pluck versus hammer-on / pull-off

labels.fitted: Second note slurred: three hammer-ons, then two pull-offs

clips.description: Five slow pairs on the Bach strings and frets. Hammer-ons: E→F♯ (2nd string, frets 5→7), G♯→B (1st, 4→7), D♯→E (1st, 11→12). Then pull-offs: E→D♯ on the 2nd string (frets 5→4, bars 4 and 6) and on the 1st (12→11, bar 10). A plucks both notes; B slurs to the second with fixed designed strengths (hammer-on: 0.7 mm fret clearance, 0.5 ms fingertip contact; pull-off: 0.6 mm sideways pull at the old fret), so its natural level differs from a pluck. The third button is the earlier legato placeholder (a small extra pluck-shaped kick), kept as a diagnostic. No real slur recording is available yet.
